explanation: No consistent trigger: fires on assorted tokens in code (MATLAB variables, require(' , version="), numbers after 'Number'/'USB'/'in', list conjunctions ('and' in drug lists), multilingual mid-word subword pieces, and prepositions. The top examples share no clear token or context feature.

Fires in text that introduces a named person (speaker, interviewee, author, professor), on the token right after the name: a pronoun 'he', a comma before a title or verb, 'to' in 'here to discuss/shed light', or subword pieces in the middle of an unusual surname. Weaker on name-like identifiers in code (RewriteRule, django.views.generic).

Fires mostly on broken or partial multibyte characters (mojibake, the middle bytes of CJK or emoji characters) and on long digit runs like '0000000'. It also fires on scattered code and math punctuation tokens ('.Text', '?,', '.*)', '\exists'). The common thread is unusual, low-frequency or garbled tokens.

Fires on long runs of whitespace (many spaces) used for column alignment inside a line: in boxed license comment headers, legal-document captions and tables of contents (between party names and docket info), and before trailing code comments. Unrelated tokens fire only weakly.

Fires very strongly on one SVG path coordinate separator (space between numbers) and moderately on separators or digits inside long numeric sequences (space- or comma-separated number lists, tables, coordinates). Elsewhere it is weak and scattered.

Strongest on the token after a long zero run in timestamp-like strings ('000000000 +0800', '000000.'). Moderately on a few code tokens and on 'en' in <html lang="en">, plus assorted mid-word subword pieces of names and medical terms. The non-top part is a mixture.

Fires on the separator right before the year in a written date: the space after 'Month Day,' or 'Month', or the '/' or '-' in numeric dates, as in tweet sign-offs and article datelines. Fires weakly on the space before a non-year number (No. 02-, 24 x 33).

Fires on the token that continues or completes a multi-token named entity or fixed phrase, such as 'Grand[ Prix]', 'Chick-fil[-A]', 'All-Century[ Team]', 'born ... 1975[ in]', 'based[ on]', '14th[ District]'. It looks like a 'predictable next part of a name or collocation' feature, but it is fairly diffuse.

Fires on tokens inside citation and markup structures (citation numbers in [@bib2], [@CR1]; percent-statistic numbers before '%'), LaTeX and code syntax tokens, and taxonomic suffixes. It is a loose mixture of structured or bracketed formal-notation contexts.

Fires on the second subword piece of a word or name that was split into pieces (Gr[imal]dis, k[un]zisoft, Sch[um]acher, gemcit[ab]ine, Rosen[qv]ist), and on later digits inside multi-digit numbers (years, versions, timestamps). Strength depends on being mid-word after a first fragment.

No clear trigger: fires on common function words and tokens in many contexts (license boilerplate 'WITHOUT'/'with this', JS '=' / 'from' / 'require', 'India'/'USA' at the end of location phrases, math variables). There is no shared feature I can see.

Fires on characters inside random alphanumeric ID strings: hashes, URL shortener slugs (pic.twitter.com/..., jsfiddle, youtube v=), tokens and keys. It fires most on a mid-string character after a few random characters. Weak on ordinary text.

Fires on a few recurring slots: 'most' in superlatives ('their most recent', 'world's most'), the package or library name after 'import'/'package'/'using namespace' (React, com, std, pandas), the '-' in bootstrap classes 'col-md-8', and 'so' in 'In doing so'. These are several separate jobs.

Fires inside source-file license and copyright header comments: comment markers ('//', ' *') at the start of header lines, '+build' directives, 'http://' in license URLs, 'the' in license clauses, 'Copyright (c)'. Elsewhere it is weak.
